topics.topic: Whether open_store must accept and securely create a missing database file or require it to already exist
questions: Must open_store require the database file to exist so os.lstat can inspect it, or must a missing database path be accepted and securely created?
Must os.lstat be required only when the database path already exists, or must open_store cease supporting creation of an absent database file?

quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory the module creates inside data_directory — the database file and its journal, the content-addressed area, the spool area, each run's spool directory, every temporary and every published file — MUST be created owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others, so that the privacy check of the next start passes on the kernel's own files (A18 rule 2).
judgement.why: T1 asks the same question as P1 on the same unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Whether open_store may create an absent database or requires it to already exist
quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory the module creates inside data_directory — the database file and its journal, the content-addressed area, the spool area, each run's spool directory, every temporary and every published file — MUST be created owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others, so that the privacy check of the next start passes on the kernel's own files (A18 rule 2).
precedent.why: The text anticipates creation of the database file but does not say how the required pre-open os.lstat handles a path that does not yet exist.

topics.topic: Whether opening the database must prevent symbolic-link following despite the prior os.lstat check
questions: Must the database file itself be opened without following symbolic links, or is the preceding os.lstat check intended to replace that requirement? An os.lstat check does not make the later SQLite open non-following and permits a link substitution between the check and the open.

quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links; a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
judgement.why: T2 asks the same question as P2 on the same unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Whether opening the database must retain an atomic no-follow guarantee after the os.lstat check
quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory under the data directory MUST be opened without following symbolic links; a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
precedent.why: The open_store-specific passage prescribes a prior os.lstat check, while the broader no-follow rule is framed for calls after start, leaving the database-opening guarantee unresolved.
